subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Identify the sentence with correct parallel structure across correlative conjunctions:
options: The lead engineer intended not only to upgrade the firmware but also to redesign the heat sink.
The lead engineer intended not only to upgrade the firmware but also redesigning the heat sink.
The lead engineer not only intended to upgrade the firmware but also redesign the heat sink.
The lead engineer intended to not only upgrade the firmware but also the heat sink was redesigned.
explanation: Both elements joined by "not only... but also" must be grammatically parallel infinitival phrases ("to upgrade..." and "to redesign...").

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Choose the sentence that correctly employs the relative pronoun "whom":
options: The visiting professor whom the committee selected delivered a lecture on quantum chromodynamics.
The visiting professor whom delivered the lecture was selected by the committee.
The visiting professor whom was recognized by the board presented the paper.
The visiting professor whom authored the textbook received the medal.
explanation: "Whom" is the objective case pronoun functioning as the direct object of the verb "selected" ("the committee selected him"). In the other options, the pronoun serves as the subject and requires "who".

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Select the sentence demonstrating correct subject-verb agreement with a collective noun functioning as unified entity:
options: The adjudication panel has reached its unanimous verdict regarding the patent infringement.
The adjudication panel have reached its unanimous verdict regarding the patent infringement.
The adjudication panel are arguing among themselves regarding the patent infringement.
The adjudication panel were unified in its decision regarding the patent infringement.
explanation: When a collective noun ("panel") acts as a single unified body with a unanimous decision, it takes a singular verb ("has reached") and singular pronoun ("its").

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Identify the sentence with correct negative adverbial inversion:
options: Seldom have high-pressure steam turbines operated under such elevated thermal gradients without failure.
Seldom high-pressure steam turbines have operated under such elevated thermal gradients without failure.
Seldom operated high-pressure steam turbines under such elevated thermal gradients without failure.
Seldom have operated high-pressure steam turbines under such elevated thermal gradients without failure.
explanation: When a sentence opens with a negative or restrictive adverb like "Seldom", standard English syntax requires subject-auxiliary inversion: "Seldom + auxiliary verb (have) + subject + main verb".

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Select the option containing a grammatically valid absolute phrase:
options: The chamber pressure having dropped below the threshold, the automated relief valve closed instantly.
Dropping below the threshold, the automated relief valve closed the chamber pressure instantly.
Because of the chamber pressure dropped below the threshold, the automated relief valve closed.
Having been dropped below the threshold, the technician closed the automated relief valve.
explanation: An absolute phrase consists of a noun ("The chamber pressure") and a participle ("having dropped..."), possessing its own subject and modifying the entire independent clause.

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Choose the grammatically accurate sentence featuring a cleft construction emphasizing the direct cause:
options: It was the sudden loss of coolant that precipitated the generator automatic shutdown.
It was the sudden loss of coolant which it precipitated the generator automatic shutdown.
There was the sudden loss of coolant that it precipitated the generator automatic shutdown.
What was the sudden loss of coolant that precipitated the generator automatic shutdown.
explanation: An "it-cleft" sentence takes the form: "It + form of to be + emphasized element + that-clause". Here, "It was the sudden loss of coolant that precipitated..." is perfectly constructed.

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Identify the sentence that correctly maintains grammatical mood and aspect without tense contamination:
options: Were the structural girder to fracture under cyclic loading, the entire cantilever truss would collapse.
Were the structural girder fracturing under cyclic loading, the entire cantilever truss will collapse.
If the structural girder would fracture under cyclic loading, the entire cantilever truss would collapse.
Were the structural girder fractured under cyclic loading, the entire cantilever truss will have collapsed.
explanation: Inverted subjunctive conditional ("Were + subject + to-infinitive") pairs strictly with conditional modal auxiliary "would + base verb" in the apodosis ("would collapse").

subject: English
question_text: Choose the word that is most nearly SYNONYMOUS with "UBIQUITOUS":
explanation: "Ubiquitous" means present, appearing, or found everywhere simultaneously; its closest synonym is "omnipresent".

subject: English
question_text: Select the word that is most nearly ANTONYMOUS to "DILIGENT":
explanation: "Diligent" means showing care and conscientiousness in work. Its direct antonym is "indolent" (lazy or idle).

subject: English
question_text: What is the closest SYNONYM for the word "LUCID" in technical prose?
explanation: "Lucid" means clear, easily understood, and completely intelligible.

subject: English
question_text: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to "EXPEDITE":
explanation: "Expedite" means to speed up or cause to happen sooner; its direct antonym is "hinder" (to delay or impede).

subject: English
question_text: Select the exact SYNONYM for "CANDID":
explanation: "Candid" means truthful, straightforward, and frank in speech or manner.

subject: English
question_text: The materials scientist characterized the novel alloy as "REFRACTORY". In physical science, this means:
options: Resistant to heat, melting, and chemical decomposition
Easily drawn into long conductive wires
explanation: "Refractory" materials retain their strength and chemical integrity at extremely high temperatures without melting or breaking down.

subject: English
question_text: Choose the most precise ANTONYM for the word "AMELIORATE":
explanation: "Ameliorate" means to make something bad or unsatisfactory better. Its antonym is "exacerbate" (to make worse or more severe).

subject: English
question_text: Select the word that is most nearly SYNONYMOUS with "RECALCITRANT":
explanation: "Recalcitrant" means stubbornly uncooperative or resistant to discipline, making "intractable" its closest synonym.

subject: English
question_text: What is the closest ANTONYM for "TACITURN"?
explanation: "Taciturn" describes a person who is habitually silent or uncommunicative. Its opposite is "loquacious" (talkative, garrulous).

subject: English
question_text: Choose the word that is most nearly SYNONYMOUS with "OBFUSCATE":
explanation: "Obfuscate" means to deliberately make something obscure, unclear, or bewildered. "Befog" (or confuse/darken) is synonymous.

subject: English
question_text: Select the most accurate ANTONYM for "CAPRICIOUS":
explanation: "Capricious" denotes unpredictable, erratic, and impulsive changes of mood or behavior. "Steadfast" (firm, resolute, unwavering) is its opposite.

subject: English
question_text: The word "PELLUCID" in literary and optical contexts means:
options: Translucently clear in presentation or transmission of light
Prone to fracturing along crystalline planes
explanation: "Pellucid" means translucently clear, easily understood, or permitting the free passage of light.

subject: English
question_text: Choose the closest ANTONYM for "PROCLIVITY":
explanation: "Proclivity" refers to a natural inclination or predisposition towards something. Its antonym is "antipathy" or aversion.

subject: English
question_text: Select the word that correctly replaces the underlined phrase: "The theoretical model was criticized for being _based on assumptions that cannot be verified or tested experimentally_."
explanation: An assertion or hypothesis that cannot be proven false through empirical observation or testing is defined as "unfalsifiable" in epistemology.

subject: English
question_text: Identify the sentence that correctly remedies the comma splice error:
options: The tensile strength of the titanium rod was tested; it exceeded all aerospace specifications.
The tensile strength of the titanium rod was tested, it exceeded all aerospace specifications.
The tensile strength of the titanium rod was tested, however it exceeded all aerospace specifications.
The tensile strength of the titanium rod was tested it exceeded all aerospace specifications.
explanation: Joining two independent clauses with only a comma creates a comma splice. A semicolon (or a coordinating conjunction with a comma) correctly separates them.

subject: English
question_text: Correct the misplaced adverb in the following sentence: "The automated system only detected three micro-faults during the twelve-hour diagnostic run."
options: The automated system detected only three micro-faults during the twelve-hour diagnostic run.
Only the automated system detected three micro-faults during the twelve-hour diagnostic run.
The automated system detected three micro-faults only during the twelve-hour diagnostic run.
During the twelve-hour diagnostic run only the automated system detected three micro-faults.
explanation: The limiting adverb "only" must immediately precede the quantity it modifies ("three micro-faults"), not the verb "detected".

subject: English
question_text: Select the sentence that eliminates grammatical disagreement in subject and verb:
options: A battery of electro-chemical tests was conducted by the quality assurance team.
A battery of electro-chemical tests were conducted by the quality assurance team.
A battery of electro-chemical tests have been conducted by the quality assurance team.
A battery of electro-chemical tests are conducted by the quality assurance team.
explanation: The head noun of the subject is the singular collective noun "battery", which requires the singular verb "was conducted".

subject: English
question_text: Identify the sentence that correctly uses the standard prepositional idiom:
options: The new solar inverter is capable of converting direct current with 98% efficiency.
The new solar inverter is capable to convert direct current with 98% efficiency.
The new solar inverter is capable in converting direct current with 98% efficiency.
The new solar inverter is capable for converting direct current with 98% efficiency.
explanation: The adjective "capable" is idiomatically followed by the preposition "of" + gerund ("capable of converting"), unlike "able", which takes an infinitive ("able to convert").

subject: English
question_text: Choose the sentence that corrects the faulty comparison: "The thermal conductivity of diamond is substantially higher than copper."
options: The thermal conductivity of diamond is substantially higher than that of copper.
The thermal conductivity of diamond is substantially higher than copper's conductivity is high.
The thermal conductivity of diamond is substantially higher as compared to copper.
The thermal conductivity of diamond is substantially higher than those of copper.
explanation: A comparison must equate like entities: the "thermal conductivity" of diamond must be compared to "that [the thermal conductivity] of copper", not the metal itself.

subject: English
question_text: Select the sentence that resolves the dangling modifier: "Having analyzed the spectral telemetry data, an unexpected Doppler shift was discovered."
options: Having analyzed the spectral telemetry data, the astrophysicist discovered an unexpected Doppler shift.
Having analyzed the spectral telemetry data, an unexpected Doppler shift appeared to the astrophysicist.
While analyzing the spectral telemetry data, an unexpected Doppler shift was discovered.
The spectral telemetry data having been analyzed, an unexpected Doppler shift was discovered by the team.
explanation: The subject performing the action of analyzing must be the grammatical subject of the main clause ("the astrophysicist"), preventing the modifier from dangling.

subject: English
question_text: In formal academic discourse, which sentence correctly demonstrates pronoun-antecedent agreement with compound antecedents?
options: Neither the chief architect nor the project engineers surrendered their professional licenses.
Neither the chief architect nor the project engineers surrendered his or her professional license.
Neither the project engineers nor the chief architect surrendered their professional licenses.
Neither the project engineers nor the chief architect surrendered their professional license.
explanation: When subjects are linked by "neither... nor", the pronoun agrees with the closer antecedent. "Project engineers" is plural, requiring the plural pronoun "their".

subject: English
question_text: Choose the option that correctly adheres to the idiom governing "prefer":
options: The aerospace firm prefers composite carbon fiber to conventional aluminum alloys.
The aerospace firm prefers composite carbon fiber than conventional aluminum alloys.
The aerospace firm prefers composite carbon fiber rather than conventional aluminum alloys.
The aerospace firm prefers composite carbon fiber over conventional aluminum alloys.
explanation: In formal English idiom, the verb "prefer" takes the preposition "to" to express preference between two nouns: "prefers X to Y".

subject: English
question_text: Select the sentence that avoids faulty predication and illogical attribution:
options: The function of an automotive thermostat is to regulate coolant flow through the engine block.
The function of an automotive thermostat is when it regulates coolant flow through the engine block.
The function of an automotive thermostat is where it regulates coolant flow through the engine block.
An automotive thermostat is because it regulates coolant flow through the engine block.
explanation: Predications defining a "function" must complete the linking verb with an infinitive phrase ("is to regulate"), avoiding colloquial constructions like "is when" or "is where".

subject: English
question_text: Identify the option that corrects both the correlative conjunction placement and grammatical parallelism:
options: The civil engineer evaluated the foundation not only for seismic resilience but also for hydrostatic resistance.
The civil engineer not only evaluated the foundation for seismic resilience but also for hydrostatic resistance.
The civil engineer evaluated the foundation not only for seismic resilience but also evaluated hydrostatic resistance.
Not only did the civil engineer evaluate the foundation for seismic resilience, but also for hydrostatic resistance.
explanation: "Not only" and "but also" must be followed by identical syntactic structures: "for seismic resilience" and "for hydrostatic resistance" (prepositional phrases).

subject: English
question_text: Select the revision that correctly resolves the faulty ellipsis in the comparative clause:
options: The prototype brushless motor generates as much torque as, if not more torque than, the commercial benchmark.
The prototype brushless motor generates as much torque, if not more torque than, the commercial benchmark.
The prototype brushless motor generates as much torque as, if not more than, the commercial benchmark.
The prototype brushless motor generates as much torque than, if not more than, the commercial benchmark.
explanation: The phrase "as much torque as" must be grammatically complete before introducing the parenthetical condition "if not more torque than". Omitting the second "as" is a faulty ellipsis.

subject: English
question_text: Choose the sentence that correctly avoids pleonasm (unnecessary semantic redundancy) while retaining precise meaning:
options: The software team reverted to the previous version to prevent system deadlock.
The software team reverted back to the previous version to prevent system deadlock.
The software team reverted back to the earlier previous version to prevent system deadlock.
The software team retroactively reverted back to the previous version to prevent system deadlock.
explanation: "Revert" already contains the meaning of going back ("re-"); saying "revert back" is redundant. Option A is concise and grammatically immaculate.

subject: English
question_text: Identify the sentence with correct handling of joint vs. separate possessive nouns:
options: Watson and Crick's seminal paper revolutionized our understanding of nucleic acid architecture.
Watson's and Crick's seminal paper revolutionized our understanding of nucleic acid architecture.
Watson and Crick seminal paper revolutionized our understanding of nucleic acid architecture.
Watson's and Crick seminal paper revolutionized our understanding of nucleic acid architecture.
explanation: When two individuals jointly author or own a single item ("seminal paper"), the possessive apostrophe is added only to the second name ("Watson and Crick's").

subject: English
question_text: Select the sentence that accurately uses the subjunctive mood in an inverted hypothetical contrary-to-fact clause:
options: Had the cooling water pumps failed, the emergency shutdown mechanism would have scrammed the core within seconds.
Had the cooling water pumps failed, the emergency shutdown mechanism had scrammed the core within seconds.
Should the cooling water pumps have failed, the emergency shutdown mechanism would scram the core within seconds.
If the cooling water pumps had failed, the emergency shutdown mechanism scrammed the core within seconds.
explanation: The inverted past contrary-to-fact conditional ("Had + subject + past participle") correctly pairs with "would have + past participle" in the result clause.

subject: English
question_text:
Read the excerpt: "Perovskite solar cells have emerged as a disruptive photovoltaic technology due to their high absorption coefficient and low fabrication cost via solution processing. However, commercial viability remains constrained by chemical degradation when exposed to moisture and ultraviolet radiation."

What is the primary obstacle to commercializing perovskite solar cells?
options: Chemical instability in ambient environmental conditions (moisture and UV)
Extremely poor absorption of incident solar photons
explanation: The passage explicitly states that commercial viability is constrained by "chemical degradation when exposed to moisture and ultraviolet radiation".

subject: English
question_text: Based on the excerpt in Question 123, what advantageous property do perovskite solar cells possess?
options: High optical absorption coefficient and economical solution processing
Complete immunity to environmental degradation and thermal stress
Mechanical flexibility exceeding that of any existing synthetic polymer
Ability to generate electricity without absorbing photons
explanation: The excerpt highlights their "high absorption coefficient and low fabrication cost via solution processing".

subject: English
question_text:
Read the excerpt: "In digital communications, Shannon's Channel Capacity theorem establishes the maximum rate at which information can be transmitted error-free across a noisy channel of given bandwidth. Attempting to transmit at rates above this theoretical capacity inevitably introduces uncorrectable bit errors."

What is the central implication of Shannon's theorem?
options: There is a fundamental mathematical upper limit to error-free transmission in noisy channels
Bandwidth can be increased infinitely without altering channel noise
Transmission errors can always be eliminated regardless of data rate
Noisy channels cannot transmit digital signals under any circumstances
explanation: The passage asserts that Shannon's theorem sets the "maximum rate at which information can be transmitted error-free", beyond which errors are inevitable.

subject: English
question_text:
Read the excerpt: "Metamaterials derive their anomalous electromagnetic properties—such as a negative refractive index—not from the chemical composition of their constituent atoms, but from the deliberate sub-wavelength geometric arrangement of their artificial inclusions."

What is the fundamental source of a metamaterial's unique properties?
options: The engineered sub-wavelength geometric structure of its inclusions
Rare earth chemical elements present in its crystalline matrix
Spontaneous atomic decay of heavy radioactive isotopes
Thermal excitation of free valence electrons
explanation: The text states that properties arise "not from the chemical composition... but from the deliberate sub-wavelength geometric arrangement of their artificial inclusions".

subject: English
question_text: In the metamaterials passage above (Question 126), the word "anomalous" most nearly means:
options: Unconventional and deviating from standard physical behavior
explanation: "Anomalous" means deviating from what is standard, normal, or expected, referring here to unconventional phenomena like negative refraction.

subject: English
question_text:
Read the excerpt: "In magnetic confinement fusion, the tokamak uses helical magnetic fields to confine high-temperature deuterium-tritium plasma. Maintaining the stability of this plasma requires mitigating magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) instabilities, which threaten to breach the vacuum vessel wall and quench the reaction."

It can be inferred from the passage that MHD instabilities:
options: Can cause plasma disruption and extinguish the thermonuclear fusion reaction
Are essential for increasing the thermal energy of deuterium ions
Strengthen the confining magnetic fields around the vacuum vessel
Prevent neutrons from escaping the reactor chamber
explanation: The passage states that instabilities "threaten to breach the vacuum vessel wall and quench the reaction" (extinguishing it).

subject: English
question_text: Referring to the fusion passage above (Question 128), what does the author imply by the word "quench"?
options: Cool down through liquid nitrogen injection
explanation: In physics and combustion contexts, to "quench" a reaction means to rapidly suppress, stifle, or extinguish it.

subject: English
question_text:
Read the excerpt: "While silicon has dominated microelectronics for over half a century, its fundamental physical scaling limit—dictated by quantum mechanical tunneling through ultra-thin gate oxides—heralds the plateau of Moore's Law. Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) offer single-atom-thick channels that effectively suppress such parasitic leakage currents."

According to the passage, why are TMDs being explored as silicon successors?
options: Their atomic thinness mitigates quantum tunneling leakage currents at nanoscale gates
They are far cheaper to extract from geological deposits than common silicon
They operate without generating any thermal resistance or heat
They completely eliminate the requirement for gate dielectric materials
explanation: The text notes that TMDs "offer single-atom-thick channels that effectively suppress such parasitic leakage currents" caused by quantum tunneling.

subject: English
question_text: In the passage regarding Moore's Law above (Question 130), the word "parasitic" describes currents that are:
options: Undesirable, wasteful leakage that undermines device performance
Essential for supplying operational voltage to the gate
Beneficial in enhancing transistor clock speed
explanation: In electronics, "parasitic" refers to unintended, harmful capacitive, inductive, or leakage effects that waste power and degrade efficiency.

subject: English
question_text:
Read the excerpt: "Quantum key distribution (QKD) leverages the fundamental quantum principle that measuring an unknown quantum state inevitably disturbs it. Consequently, any eavesdropping adversary attempting to intercept photons transmitted across an optical fiber inevitably introduces detectable quantum bit error rates (QBER), alerting the communicating parties."

What provides the fundamental security guarantee in QKD systems?
options: Laws of quantum mechanics that mandate measurement introduces disturbance
Physical isolation of fibers inside impenetrable concrete conduits
Electromagnetic shielding that blocks all external radio signals
explanation: Security rests on the physical principle that "measuring an unknown quantum state inevitably disturbs it", creating detectable error rates.

subject: English
question_text:
Read the excerpt: "Epistemological reductionism posits that complex biological systems can be comprehensively understood by analyzing their isolated molecular constituents. However, systems biologists counter that emergent properties—phenomena arising strictly from nonlinear interactions among networked elements—preclude complete explanatory reductionism."

Which statement best captures the philosophical conflict presented in the passage?
options: Whether macroscopic biological phenomena can be fully deduced from isolated molecular parts or require holistic system-level analysis
Whether biological organisms obey standard thermodynamic conservation laws
Whether empirical observation is superior to deductive mathematical modeling in genetics
Whether molecular biology should be discarded in favor of evolutionary taxonomy
explanation: The passage contrasts reductionism (understanding systems via isolated parts) with systems biology (emergent properties requiring holistic, networked analysis).

subject: English
question_text: In the systems biology passage above (Question 133), what does the term "emergent properties" denote?
options: Novel characteristics that manifest only at the collective level due to nonlinear element interactions
Properties that disappear as an organism reaches developmental maturity
Simple additive sums of the properties of isolated individual components
Imperfections introduced by experimental measuring apparatus
explanation: Emergent properties are systemic attributes arising from interactions between system components that cannot be predicted simply by analyzing parts in isolation.

subject: English
question_text:
Read the excerpt: "The anthropic cosmological principle observes that the physical constants of our universe—such as the fine-structure constant and cosmological constant—fall within an infinitesimally narrow range permitting the synthesis of carbon and the subsequent evolution of sentient observers. Proponents of the multiverse hypothesis contend that this apparent fine-tuning is merely an observer selection effect across an ensemble of universes."

According to the multiverse proponent viewpoint described in the passage:
options: We inevitably observe finely tuned constants because observers can only exist in universes hospitable to life
Our universe was deliberately engineered by conscious entities to foster carbon life
The fine-structure constant changes value unpredictably over cosmological epochs
Carbon-based life can flourish regardless of the values of fundamental physical constants
explanation: The multiverse hypothesis explains fine-tuning as an "observer selection effect" (we can only observe a universe whose constants permit observers to exist).

subject: English
question_text: The author's tone in describing the anthropic principle and the multiverse hypothesis in Question 135 is best characterized as:
explanation: The author presents the competing scientific and philosophical arguments dispassionately and neutrally, demonstrating an objective and analytical tone.

subject: English
question_text:
Select the pair that best expresses a relationship similar to the original:
THERMAL : HEAT ::
explanation: "Thermal" relates to heat, just as "acoustic" relates to sound (adjective indicating relationship to the respective physical phenomenon).

subject: English
question_text:
Choose the matching pair:
HYGROMETER : HUMIDITY ::
explanation: A hygrometer is an instrument specifically designed to measure humidity, just as an anemometer measures wind speed.

subject: English
question_text:
Complete the analogy:
MALLEABLE : COMPRESSION ::
explanation: Malleability is the capacity of a material to deform plastically under compressive stress, while ductility is the ability to deform under tensile stress (tension).

subject: English
question_text:
Identify the analogous pair:
CONCAVE : CONVEX ::
explanation: A concave lens/mirror acts as a diverging optical element, whereas a convex element acts as a converging element, establishing a complementary geometric and functional opposition.

subject: English
question_text:
Select the best matching relationship:
FUSE : OVERCURRENT ::
explanation: A fuse mitigates and protects against harmful electrical overcurrent, just as a shock absorber mitigates harmful mechanical vibration.

subject: English
question_text:
Complete the analogy:
CATALYST : ACTIVATION ENERGY ::
explanation: A catalyst lowers the activation energy barrier of a chemical reaction, just as a lubricant reduces the frictional resistance between sliding surfaces.

subject: English
question_text:
Select the matching pair:
PRISM : DISPERSION ::
explanation: A prism decomposes polychromatic light into its spectrum via dispersion, just as a diffraction grating decomposes light via interference and diffraction.

subject: English
question_text:
Choose the pair expressing the same relationship:
VOLTAGE : CURRENT ::
explanation: In fluid mechanics (Poiseuille's law) and electrical circuits (Ohm's law), voltage is the driving potential difference driving electric current, analogous to pressure gradient driving fluid flow rate.

subject: English
question_text:
Identify the matching pair:
OSMOSIS : CONCENTRATION GRADIENT ::
explanation: Osmosis is the net transport of solvent driven by a chemical potential/concentration gradient, just as thermal conduction is heat transfer driven by a temperature gradient (Fourier's law).

subject: English
question_text:
Select the pair that best mirrors the relationship:
ZENITH : NADIR ::
explanation: "Zenith" (highest celestial point directly overhead) and "nadir" (lowest point directly below) are diametrically opposed celestial coordinates, identical to "apogee" (farthest orbital point) and "perigee" (closest orbital point).

subject: English
question_text:
Complete the analogy:
SUPERFLUOUS : SURPLUS ::
explanation: Something "superfluous" is characterized by excess or surplus, just as something "vacuous" is characterized by emptiness or inanity.

subject: English
question_text:
Choose the pair expressing the same relationship:
TENACIOUS : YIELD ::
explanation: A "tenacious" entity refuses to yield or surrender, just as an "impervious" barrier refuses to let substances penetrate it (quality defined by resistance to the action).

subject: English
question_text:
Select the matching pair:
INERTIA : ACCELERATION ::
explanation: Inertia is a body's intrinsic resistance to a change in velocity (acceleration), just as capacitance is an electrical element's resistance to sudden changes in voltage across it (i = C dv/dt).

subject: English
question_text:
Identify the analogous pair:
METASTABLE : PERTURBATION ::
explanation: A metastable state remains stable only until subjected to a slight perturbation that triggers transition to lower energy, analogous to a precarious position that collapses upon experiencing a minor disturbance.

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Identify the part of speech of the capitalized word in the sentence: "She spoke ELOQUENTLY during the international symposium."
explanation: "Eloquently" is an adverb modifying the verb "spoke", describing the manner in which the speech was delivered.

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition: "The candidate was fully confident _____ her performance in the competitive entrance exam."
explanation: The standard idiomatic adjective-preposition collocation is "confident of" (or "confident in" someone/something; here "confident of her performance" is the prescribed standard English usage).

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Select the correct tense form to complete the sentence: "By the time the keynote speaker arrived, the auditorium _____ completely."
explanation: When two past actions are related chronologically, the earlier action is expressed in the past perfect tense ("had filled") relative to the simple past ("arrived").

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Choose the appropriate article to complete the sentence: "He is _____ honorable gentleman who values academic integrity."
explanation: "Honorable" begins with a silent "h" and a vowel sound (/ˈɒn.ər.ə.bəl/), thus taking the indefinite article "an".

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: What is the grammatical function of the gerund phrase in the sentence: "SWIMMING IN TURBULENT WATERS requires substantial endurance"?
explanation: The gerund phrase "Swimming in turbulent waters" acts as the noun subject governing the singular predicate "requires".

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Select the sentence displaying correct subject-verb agreement with correlative conjunctions:
options: Neither the principal investigator nor the research assistants were aware of the calibration error.
Neither the principal investigator nor the research assistants was aware of the calibration error.
Neither the research assistants nor the principal investigator were aware of the calibration error.
Neither the research assistants or the principal investigator was aware of the calibration error.
explanation: Under the rule of proximity for "neither... nor", the verb agrees in number with the closer subject ("research assistants" is plural, so "were aware" is correct).

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Convert the following direct speech into reported speech correctly: "The professor said, 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius under standard atmospheric pressure.'"
options: The professor said that water boils at 100 degrees Celsius under standard atmospheric pressure.
The professor said that water boiled at 100 degrees Celsius under standard atmospheric pressure.
The professor said that water had boiled at 100 degrees Celsius under standard atmospheric pressure.
The professor told that water would boil at 100 degrees Celsius under standard atmospheric pressure.
explanation: Universal scientific truths and general physical facts remain in the simple present tense even when the reporting verb is in the past tense.

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Identify the sentence that correctly employs the subjunctive mood:
options: The committee recommended that the draft protocol be submitted for institutional review immediately.
The committee recommended that the draft protocol is submitted for institutional review immediately.
The committee recommended that the draft protocol was submitted for institutional review immediately.
The committee recommended that the draft protocol should had been submitted for institutional review immediately.
explanation: Verbs of demand, recommendation, or urgency require the mandative subjunctive form (base verb "be submitted"), without "is", "was", or modal auxiliaries.

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Which sentence correctly uses an inversion construction after a negative restrictive adverbial?
options: Seldom have we witnessed such a profound paradigm shift in theoretical physics.
Seldom we have witnessed such a profound paradigm shift in theoretical physics.
Seldom we witnessed such a profound paradigm shift in theoretical physics.
Seldom had we witness such a profound paradigm shift in theoretical physics.
explanation: When a negative or restrictive adverbial (like "seldom", "rarely", "scarcely") is placed sentence-initially for emphasis, subject-auxiliary inversion is mandatory ("have we witnessed").

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Identify the type of dependent clause in the sentence: "Although the experimental setup was intricate, the team gathered conclusive empirical data."
explanation: The subordinate clause introduced by "although" is an adverbial clause of concession indicating a contrasting condition to the main clause.

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Analyze the syntactic structure of the capitalized clause: "It is imperative THAT EVERY RESEARCHER COMPLY WITH LABORATORY BIO-SAFETY STANDARDS."
options: Substantive noun clause functioning as the delayed true subject of the sentence with mandative subjunctive verb
Adjectival relative clause modifying the dummy pronoun "It"
Adverbial clause of purpose with an indicative verb
Prepositional complement clause functioning as an adjunct
explanation: "It" is an expletive (dummy) pronoun; the capitalized "that"-clause is a nominal content clause functioning as the extraposed real subject, employing the mandative subjunctive verb "comply".

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Choose the sentence that correctly utilizes an absolute phrase without dangling or syntactic detachment:
options: The empirical tests having yielded ambiguous outcomes, the laboratory scheduled an independent peer audit.
Having yielded ambiguous outcomes, an independent peer audit was scheduled by the laboratory.
The laboratory scheduled an audit, the tests were ambiguous.
The empirical tests having yielded ambiguous outcomes, it was decided to cancel the project.
explanation: "The empirical tests having yielded ambiguous outcomes" is a grammatically legitimate nominative absolute phrase containing its own subject ("tests") and participle ("having yielded"), modifying the entire independent clause.

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Select the option that correctly represents the passive transformation of the ditransitive sentence: "The panel awarded Dr. Alvi the lifetime achievement medal in biophysics."
options: Dr. Alvi was awarded the lifetime achievement medal in biophysics by the panel.
The lifetime achievement medal in biophysics was being awarded Dr. Alvi by the panel.
Dr. Alvi had been awarding the lifetime achievement medal in biophysics by the panel.
The lifetime achievement medal in biophysics was awarded of Dr. Alvi by the panel.
explanation: In transforming a ditransitive clause, making the indirect object ("Dr. Alvi") the passive subject gives: "Dr. Alvi was awarded the lifetime achievement medal in biophysics by the panel."

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Which sentence exhibits a non-finite catenative complementation pattern with an accusative and infinitive structure?
options: The senior engineer observed the turbine rotate at supersonic angular velocity.
The senior engineer was observing that the turbine rotates at supersonic velocity.
The rotation of the turbine at supersonic velocity was observed.
Having observed the turbine, the senior engineer recorded the velocity.
explanation: Verbs of perception like "observe", "watch", and "hear" take a bare infinitive complement after an accusative noun phrase ("observed [the turbine] [rotate]").

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Identify the sentence containing a correctly structured third conditional inverted construction (omission of "if"):
options: Had the cooling mechanism not malfunctioned, the secondary containment vessel would have remained intact.
Should the cooling mechanism not malfunction, the secondary containment vessel would remain intact.
Were the cooling mechanism not to malfunction, the secondary containment vessel would have remained intact.
Had not the cooling mechanism malfunctioned, the secondary containment vessel would remain intact.
explanation: Inverted third conditional clauses invert auxiliary "had" with the subject: "Had the cooling mechanism not malfunctioned...". Note that the contraction "Hadn't" or full "Had [subject] not" is required.

subject: English
question_text: Choose the most accurate SYNONYM for the word "METICULOUS":
explanation: "Meticulous" means showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise. "Painstaking" is its direct synonym.

subject: English
question_text: Choose the most accurate ANTONYM for the word "LUCID":
explanation: "Lucid" means clear and easy to understand; its antonym is "obscure" (unclear or difficult to perceive).

subject: English
question_text: What is the meaning of the word "BENEVOLENT" as used in academic discourse?
options: Well-meaning and kindly disposed toward others
explanation: "Benevolent" derives from Latin roots meaning wishing well, characterized by kindness and charitable goodwill.

subject: English
question_text: Choose the most accurate SYNONYM for the word "PRAGMATIC":
explanation: "Pragmatic" means dealing with matters realistically based on practical rather than theoretical considerations.

subject: English
question_text: Choose the most accurate ANTONYM for the word "CANDID":
explanation: "Candid" means truthful and straightforward; its opposite is "deceitful" or disingenuous.

subject: English
question_text: Select the most appropriate SYNONYM for the word "EPHEMERAL":
explanation: "Ephemeral" means lasting for a very short time; "transient" conveys the exact same fleeting temporality.

subject: English
question_text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM for the word "VORACIOUS":
explanation: "Voracious" means possessing an insatiable appetite or eagerness. "Abstemious" describes moderate and sparing consumption, serving as its antonym.

subject: English
question_text: Which word best completes the sentence: "The speaker's arguments were so _____ that even the most skeptical members of the jury conceded the thesis"?
explanation: "Cogent" means clear, logical, and powerfully convincing.

subject: English
question_text: Choose the most accurate SYNONYM for the word "UBIQUITOUS":
explanation: "Ubiquitous" means present, appearing, or found everywhere simultaneously; "omnipresent" is its direct synonym.

subject: English
question_text: Choose the most accurate ANTONYM for the word "TENACIOUS":
explanation: "Tenacious" means holding firm or persistent; its antonym is "yielding" or compliant.

subject: English
question_text: Choose the most precise SYNONYM for the word "TRUCULENT":
explanation: "Truculent" means aggressively defiant, eager to argue, or belligerent.

subject: English
question_text: Select the most accurate ANTONYM for the word "ESOTERIC":
explanation: "Esoteric" means intended for or understood by only an enlightened inner circle; its true etymological antonym is "exoteric" (suitable for or understood by the general public).

subject: English
question_text: What is the contextual meaning of "PUSILLANIMOUS" in a philosophical treatise on moral courage?
options: Timid and lacking courage in the face of danger
explanation: "Pusillanimous" comes from Latin "pusillus" (very small) + "animus" (mind/spirit), signifying cowardice, faint-heartedness, or lack of resolve.

subject: English
question_text: Identify the word whose meaning is closest to "INCHOATE":
options: Rudimentary and just beginning to develop
explanation: "Inchoate" means only recently begun and not fully formed, organized, or developed; rudimentary.

subject: English
question_text: Choose the pair that represents an accurate ANTONYM relationship for "EQUANIMITY":
explanation: "Equanimity" denotes mental calmness and composure under psychological pressure; its antonym is "agitation" or disquiet.

subject: English
question_text: Identify the sentence free from grammatical errors:
options: Each of the newly designed solar modules undergoes rigorous durability testing.
Each of the newly designed solar modules undergo rigorous durability testing.
Each of the newly designed solar modules are undergoing rigorous durability testing.
Each of the newly designed solar modules have undergone rigorous durability testing.
explanation: The pronoun "each" is singular and takes a singular verb ("undergoes"), irrespective of the plural prepositional complement ("of the modules").

subject: English
question_text: Choose the grammatically correct sentence:
options: Neither the professor nor her students were able to replicate the anomalous result.
Neither the professor nor her students was able to replicate the anomalous result.
Neither the professor or her students were able to replicate the anomalous result.
Neither the professor nor her students is able to replicate the anomalous result.
explanation: With "neither... nor", the verb agrees with the closer subject ("students" is plural, requiring "were able").

subject: English
question_text: Identify the sentence that correctly corrects the misplaced modifier: "Walking into the laboratory, the smoke was seen by the technician."
options: Walking into the laboratory, the technician saw the smoke.
Walking into the laboratory, smoke was seeing by the technician.
The smoke saw the technician, walking into the laboratory.
While walking into the laboratory, the smoke became visible to the technician.
explanation: The dangling participle "Walking into the laboratory" logically modifies the person performing the action ("the technician"), who must immediately follow the introductory phrase.

subject: English
question_text: Which sentence maintains correct comparative degree usage?
options: This algorithmic framework is more efficient than any other method currently deployed.
This algorithmic framework is more efficient than any method currently deployed.
This algorithmic framework is most efficient than any method currently deployed.
This algorithmic framework is more efficiently than any other method currently deployed.
explanation: When comparing an item to members of its own group, "any other" must be used to exclude the item itself from the comparison group.

subject: English
question_text: Select the sentence that contains NO punctuation or comma-splice error:
options: The thermal sensors registered an abrupt spike; consequently, the automated shutdown triggered.
The thermal sensors registered an abrupt spike, consequently, the automated shutdown triggered.
The thermal sensors registered an abrupt spike consequently the automated shutdown triggered.
The thermal sensors registered an abrupt spike; consequently the automated shutdown triggered.
explanation: A conjunctive adverb ("consequently") joining two independent clauses must be preceded by a semicolon and followed by a comma.

subject: English
question_text: Choose the sentence that exhibits correct parallel structure:
options: The aerospace program aims to improve propulsion efficiency, reduce fuel consumption, and enhance payload safety.
The aerospace program aims to improve propulsion efficiency, reducing fuel consumption, and to enhance payload safety.
The aerospace program aims at improving propulsion efficiency, reduction of fuel, and enhances payload safety.
The aerospace program aims to improve propulsion efficiency, to reduce fuel consumption, and enhancing payload safety.
explanation: Series items must share identical grammatical form: "to improve..., reduce..., and enhance..." (parallel base verbs governed by "to").

subject: English
question_text: Select the sentence that avoids faulty pronoun reference:
options: Although the software suite had numerous vulnerabilities, the cybersecurity team patched all of them before deployment.
Although the software suite had numerous vulnerabilities, the cybersecurity team patched it all before deployment.
When the software met with vulnerabilities, they patched them quickly.
In the software, it had vulnerabilities that the team patched.
explanation: "Them" unambiguously refers to the plural antecedent "vulnerabilities", avoiding the vague pronoun references seen in the other options.

subject: English
question_text: Identify the sentence with correct idiom and prepositional usage:
options: The regulatory board insisted on compliance with the updated safety statutes.
The regulatory board insisted to comply with the updated safety statutes.
The regulatory board insisted for compliance on the updated safety statutes.
The regulatory board insisted at compliance of the updated safety statutes.
explanation: The verb "insisted" takes the preposition "on" ("insisted on"), and "compliance" collocates with "with" ("compliance with safety statutes").

subject: English
question_text: Choose the sentence that corrects the faulty comparison in: "The computational power of modern quantum processors exceeds classical supercomputers."
options: The computational power of modern quantum processors exceeds that of classical supercomputers.
The computational power of modern quantum processors exceeds classical supercomputers themselves.
Modern quantum processors exceed computational power of classical supercomputers.
The computational power of modern quantum processors is exceeding than classical supercomputers.
explanation: A quality ("computational power") cannot be compared directly to an object ("classical supercomputers"). The demonstrative pronoun "that of" must be inserted to balance the comparison.

subject: English
question_text: Which sentence correctly avoids redundancy (pleonasm)?
options: The research consortium decided to consolidate the disparate experimental datasets into a unified archive.
The research consortium decided to consolidate the disparate experimental datasets together into a unified archive.
The research consortium decided to merge together the disparate datasets into a unified archive.
The research consortium decided to consolidate and combine together the experimental datasets.
explanation: "Consolidate" inherently means combining into a single whole; adding "together" is redundant.

subject: English
question_text: Identify the sentence that correctly resolves all issues of case, agreement, and parallelism:
options: The provost invited whoever demonstrated scholarly rigor to apply for the prestigious postdoctoral fellowship.
The provost invited whomever demonstrated scholarly rigor to apply for the prestigious postdoctoral fellowship.
The provost invited whoever demonstrates scholarly rigor to have applied for the prestigious fellowship.
The provost invited whomever had demonstrated scholarly rigor for applying to the fellowship.
explanation: The pronoun serves as the subject of the subordinate noun clause ("whoever demonstrated scholarly rigor"), not the direct object of "invited". The entire clause functions as the direct object, so the nominative case "whoever" is strictly required.

subject: English
question_text: Which sentence correctly avoids a dangling elliptical clause?
options: While conducting the spectroscopic assay, Dr. Tahir noted an unexpected fluorescence absorption peak.
While conducting the spectroscopic assay, an unexpected fluorescence absorption peak was noted.
While conducting the spectroscopic assay, the spectrum showed an absorption peak.
While in the spectroscopic assay, the absorption peak surprised Dr. Tahir.
explanation: In the elliptical clause "While conducting...", the implied subject must be identical to the grammatical subject of the main clause ("Dr. Tahir"). In passive constructions, the clause dangles.

subject: English
question_text: Select the sentence that correctly employs the subjunctive and inversion without stylistic infelicity:
options: Were the tensile strain to exceed critical thresholds, under no circumstances should the structural load be increased.
Were the tensile strain to exceed critical thresholds, under no circumstances the structural load should be increased.
If the tensile strain would exceed critical thresholds, under no circumstances should the load be increased.
Had the tensile strain exceeded critical thresholds, under no circumstances the load should be increased.
explanation: The conditional uses correct inverted subjunctive ("Were the tensile strain to exceed..."), and the negative restrictive adjunct ("under no circumstances") correctly triggers subject-auxiliary inversion ("should the structural load be increased").

subject: English
question_text: Choose the sentence that correctly pairs correlatives and adheres strictly to parallelism:
options: The newly discovered catalyst not only accelerates reaction kinetics but also minimizes thermal dissipation.
The newly discovered catalyst not only accelerates reaction kinetics but it minimizes thermal dissipation also.
Not only the catalyst accelerates reaction kinetics, but also minimizes thermal dissipation.
The newly discovered catalyst accelerates not only reaction kinetics but also it minimizes thermal dissipation.
explanation: The correlative pair "not only [verb phrase] but also [verb phrase]" balances two parallel active verbs: "accelerates reaction kinetics" and "minimizes thermal dissipation".

subject: English
question_text: Identify the sentence free from the error of faulty predication:
options: The rationale behind adopting graphene electrodes is that their high surface area enhances capacitive charge storage.
The rationale behind adopting graphene electrodes is because their high surface area enhances capacitive charge storage.
The reason behind adopting graphene electrodes is on account of their high surface area.
The rationale behind adopting graphene electrodes is due to high surface area.
explanation: "The rationale/reason is that..." is the grammatically correct predicate noun clause construction. "The reason is because/due to" is a classic error of faulty predication and tautology.

subject: English
question_text: According to the passage on thermodynamics, what must happen to the total entropy of an isolated system over time?
options: It must increase, approaching thermodynamic equilibrium
It decreases linearly as temperature drops
It remains strictly constant at all times
It fluctuates unpredictably without any net direction
explanation: The passage explicitly states: "The Second Law posits that the total entropy of an isolated system must increase over time, approaching a state of maximum thermodynamic equilibrium."

subject: English
question_text: Based on the passage, what enables localized entropy decreases in biological systems?
options: A compensatory increase in the entropy of the surrounding universe
A complete suspension of the Second Law of Thermodynamics
The total absence of heat dissipation
The perpetual creation of new mass
explanation: The passage states that localized entropy decreases occur "strictly at the thermodynamic expense of increasing the entropy of the surrounding universe."

subject: English
question_text: What is the primary subject matter of the passage?
options: The fundamental constraints imposed by the Second Law of Thermodynamics on spontaneous processes
Methods for industrial synthesis of plastics
The historical biography of Rudolf Clausius
explanation: The text focuses entirely on how the Second Law of Thermodynamics and entropy govern spontaneous physical and biological transformations.

subject: English
question_text: The word "spontaneous" in the first sentence most nearly means:
options: Occurring naturally without continuous external intervention
explanation: In thermodynamic context, "spontaneous" describes processes that occur without requiring continuous external energy input.

subject: English
question_text: Which example of a localized entropy decrease is explicitly provided in the text?
options: The expansion of an ideal gas
explanation: The author explicitly mentions "the self-assembly of biological macromolecules" as an example of localized entropy decrease.

subject: English
question_text: What fundamental shift in artificial intelligence methodology is outlined in the second passage?
options: From manually engineered heuristic rules to automated deep representation learning
From gradient optimization to mechanical calculating engines
From medical diagnostics to avionics exclusively
From statistical modeling to purely philosophical inquiry
explanation: The opening line specifies the paradigm shift "from hand-crafted heuristic rules toward deep representation learning."

subject: English
question_text: Why does the author characterize deep neural networks as an "epistemic black box"?
options: Because millions of non-linear parameter interactions obscure the transparency and interpretability of their internal reasoning
Because they operate without any electricity or computational hardware
Because their source code is kept confidential by commercial entities
Because they can only process images of black boxes
explanation: The text links the "epistemic black box" directly to "the millions of non-linear parameter interactions" that sacrifice interpretability.

subject: English
question_text: In the passage, the word "efficacy" is closest in meaning to:
explanation: "Efficacy" refers to the ability to produce a desired or intended result; effectiveness.

subject: English
question_text: Which of the following can be inferred regarding safety-critical domains from the passage?
options: Lack of interpretability hinders the validation and trustworthy adoption of deep learning models in high-stakes fields
Diagnostic medicine has completely abandoned artificial intelligence
Heuristic systems are mathematically proven to be superior in accuracy
Gradient optimization is impossible in avionics
explanation: The passage highlights that the black-box nature poses "profound validation challenges in safety-critical domains such as automated avionics and diagnostic medicine."

subject: English
question_text: What is the author's primary tone in discussing deep representation learning?
explanation: The author acknowledges the remarkable empirical efficacy of deep learning while objectively weighing its severe interpretability and validation challenges.

subject: English
question_text: According to the third passage, how does general relativity relate conceptually to Newtonian mechanics?
options: It subsumes Newtonian mechanics as a valid asymptotic limiting case under weak gravity and low velocity
It entirely refutes all predictive calculations of Newtonian gravitation as historical fiction
It proves that Newtonian equations are mathematically incompatible with any physical reality
It replaces calculus with purely non-Euclidean geometric philosophy
explanation: The author notes that relativity "circumscribed its domain" and that mature theories survive as "limiting cases of more expansive frameworks" via the correspondence principle.

subject: English
question_text: The phrase "progressive conceptual subsumption" implies that scientific progress occurs primarily through:
options: The incorporation and preservation of established models within broader, higher-level explanatory structures
The random destruction of previous scientific literature
Sudden political shifts in scientific funding
The strict rejection of all mathematical formalism
explanation: Subsumption refers to integrating or absorbing existing valid concepts into a more comprehensive framework that accounts for a wider spectrum of phenomena.

subject: English
question_text: In the passage, the word "circumscribed" most accurately denotes:
explanation: "Circumscribe" means to draw a boundary around or define the specific limits of something.

subject: English
question_text: Which philosophical view of scientific development does the author explicitly argue AGAINST?
options: The view that scientific revolutions represent wanton epistemic ruptures that discard all prior knowledge
The asymptotic convergence of physical equations
The existence of relativistic spacetime curvature
explanation: The author states: "scientific revolutions are characterized not by wanton epistemic rupture, but by progressive conceptual subsumption."

subject: English
question_text: What role does the "correspondence principle" play in the author's thesis?
options: It serves as the formal mathematical mechanism demonstrating how a new theory reduces to the old theory in familiar regimes
It mandates that scientists correspond via peer-reviewed postal journals
It proves that gravitational fields are fundamentally identical to electromagnetic waves
It demonstrates the impossibility of reconciling quantum mechanics with general relativity
explanation: The passage explains that "relativistic equations asymptotically reduce to their Newtonian counterparts via the correspondence principle."

subject: English
question_text: ANEMOMETER : WIND SPEED :: GALVANOMETER : ?
explanation: An anemometer is an instrument measuring wind speed; a galvanometer is an instrument detecting and measuring small electric currents and their direction.

subject: English
question_text: TELESCOPE : ASTRONOMER :: MICROSCOPE : ?
explanation: A telescope is the quintessential optical tool used by an astronomer; a microscope is the quintessential tool used by a microbiologist.

subject: English
question_text: INHIBITOR : BIOCHEMICAL ENZYME :: BRAKE : ?
explanation: An enzyme inhibitor retards or halts enzymatic catalytic activity; a mechanical brake slows down or stops vehicle motion.

subject: English
question_text: AUTHOR : NOVEL :: COMPOSER : ?
explanation: An author creates a novel; a composer creates a musical symphony.

subject: English
question_text: INSULATOR : ELECTRICITY :: CONDENSER : ?
explanation: An insulator impedes or confines electricity; a condenser concentrates or liquefies vapor (device/process relationship).

subject: English
question_text: IMPEDANCE : ALTERNATING CURRENT :: FRICTION : ?
explanation: Electrical impedance opposes the flow of alternating current; mechanical friction opposes translational physical motion.

subject: English
question_text: EPILOGUE : NOVEL :: CODA : ?
explanation: An epilogue is a concluding section that rounds out a literary novel; a coda is a concluding musical passage that resolves a composition.

subject: English
question_text: OSMOSIS : CONCENTRATION GRADIENT :: CURRENT : ?
explanation: Osmotic solvent movement is driven down a chemical concentration gradient; electric current flow is driven by an electric potential difference (voltage gradient).

subject: English
question_text: MUTATION : GENOME :: ERRATUM : ?
explanation: A mutation is an error or variation in a biological genome; an erratum is an error or misprint in a printed book.

subject: English
question_text: FRACTURE : BONE :: FISSURE : ?
explanation: A fracture is a crack or structural break in a bone; a fissure is a crack or narrow split in a geological rock mass.

subject: English
question_text: SYLLOGISM : LOGIC :: EXPERIMENT : ?
explanation: A syllogism is the fundamental deductive structure of formal logic; an experiment is the fundamental operational instrument of scientific empiricism.

subject: English
question_text: PROLEGOMENON : TREATISE :: PREAMBLE : ?
explanation: A prolegomenon is a formal introductory discourse preceding a scholarly treatise; a preamble is an introductory statement declaring the intent and values of a constitution.

subject: English
question_text: APOCRYPHAL : CANONICITY :: SPURIOUS : ?
explanation: "Apocryphal" denotes lacking religious canonicity or verified authority; "spurious" denotes lacking genuine authenticity or validity.

subject: English
question_text: QUINTESSENTIAL : EMBODIMENT :: PARADIGMATIC : ?
explanation: "Quintessential" describes the purest embodiment of a quality; "paradigmatic" describes serving as a quintessential model or exemplar.

subject: English
question_text: HEURISTIC : DISCOVERY :: ALGORITHM : ?
explanation: A heuristic is an exploratory practical method guiding open discovery; an algorithm is a rigorous, finite step-by-step rule ensuring deterministic computation.

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Select the correct form of the verb: "Neither the professor nor the students ______ able to solve the anomalous equation."
explanation: When compound subjects are joined by "neither... nor", the verb agrees with the closer subject ("students", which is plural, hence "were").

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Identify the part of speech of the word "swiftly" in: "The mercury in the thermometer dropped swiftly after sunset."
explanation: "Swiftly" modifies the verb "dropped", indicating manner, making it an adverb.

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition: "The research team congratulated him ______ his remarkable discovery in quantum cryptography."
explanation: The verb "congratulate" idiomatically takes the preposition "on" (congratulate someone on something).

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Choose the sentence that correctly utilizes an apostrophe for plural possession:
options: The engineers' blueprints were submitted before the regulatory deadline.
The engineer's blueprints were submitted by all six departments.
The engineers blueprint's were submitted yesterday.
explanation: For regular plural nouns ending in "s", plural possession is shown by adding an apostrophe after the "s" (engineers').

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Select the correct pronoun: "Between you and ______, the experimental results contradict the initial hypothesis."
explanation: "Between" is a preposition requiring objective case pronouns ("you and me", not "you and I").

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Identify the grammatical mood used in: "If the algorithm were more efficient, runtime would decrease by an order of magnitude."
explanation: "Were" expresses a hypothetical, counterfactual condition contrary to fact, which is the past subjunctive mood.

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Convert to indirect speech: The researcher said, "Did you calibrate the spectrophotometer this morning?"
options: The researcher asked if I had calibrated the spectrophotometer that morning.
The researcher asked if I calibrated the spectrophotometer this morning.
The researcher asked that whether I have calibrated the spectrophotometer that morning.
The researcher asked if had I calibrated the spectrophotometer that morning.
explanation: In reporting past simple questions, the tense shifts back to past perfect ("had calibrated"), "this morning" becomes "that morning", and word order becomes affirmative.

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Which sentence correctly demonstrates the use of a relative restrictive clause?
options: The catalyst that was synthesized in our laboratory accelerated the reaction rate threefold.
The catalyst, that was synthesized in our laboratory, accelerated the reaction rate threefold.
The catalyst which synthesized in our laboratory accelerating the reaction rate threefold.
The catalyst, which was synthesized in our laboratory accelerated the reaction rate threefold.
explanation: Restrictive relative clauses use "that" without surrounding commas to identify specifically which catalyst is meant.

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Choose the correct form to complete the sentence: "Hardly ______ the data analysis when a sudden power surge rebooted the central mainframe."
explanation: Negative adverbs like "hardly", "scarcely", or "seldom" at the start of a clause trigger subject-auxiliary inversion ("Hardly had the analysts initiated... when...").

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Identify the function of the underlined gerund phrase: "<u>Optimizing matrix multiplication routines</u> required specialized GPU hardware."
explanation: The gerund phrase "Optimizing matrix multiplication routines" serves as the grammatical subject of the main verb "required".

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: In formal syntax, which sentence correctly demonstrates the present subjunctive mandatory construction following a verb of demand?
options: The committee insisted that the chief architect submit the audited safety schematics immediately.
The committee insisted that the chief architect submits the audited safety schematics immediately.
The committee insisted that the chief architect will submit the audited safety schematics immediately.
The committee insisted that the chief architect should have submitted the audited safety schematics immediately.
explanation: Verbs of demand or requirement (insist, demand, recommend) take a mandative subjunctive clause with the base form of the verb ("submit", not "submits").

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Identify the structural type of the following sentence: "Although the numerical simulation converged rapidly, anomalies emerged in the boundary layer calculations, so the aerospace team recalibrated the mesh."
explanation: It contains one dependent clause ("Although the numerical simulation converged rapidly") and two independent clauses joined by coordinating conjunction "so", qualifying as compound-complex.

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Which sentence correctly adheres to the syntactic rule of maintaining parallel structure with correlative conjunctions ("not only... but also")?
options: The proposed framework not only minimizes latency across nodes but also maximizes network throughput.
The proposed framework not only minimizes latency across nodes but throughput is also maximized.
The proposed framework minimizes not only latency across nodes but also maximizing network throughput.
Not only the proposed framework minimizes latency across nodes but also it maximizes throughput.
explanation: Both elements following "not only" and "but also" must be grammatically parallel: verb phrase ("minimizes...") followed by verb phrase ("maximizes...").

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Identify the error in tense sequence: "Had Newton not formulated the laws of classical mechanics, subsequent astrophysicists ______ unable to compute planetary trajectories accurately."
explanation: In a third (past counterfactual) conditional ("Had Newton not formulated..."), the apodosis (result clause) requires "would have + past participle" ("would have been").

subject: English
subtopic: Grammar (tenses, parts of speech, sentence structure)
question_text: Which of the following contains an absolute construction (nominative absolute)?
options: The thermal limits having been breached, the containment system automatically shut down the reactor.
Having breached the thermal limits, the automated system shut down the reactor.
Breaching thermal limits is dangerous for the nuclear reactor core.
The containment system shut down after breaching the thermal limits.
explanation: An absolute phrase consists of a noun ("thermal limits") and a participle ("having been breached") with no grammatical connection to the main clause, modifying the whole sentence.

subject: English
question_text: Choose the word closest in meaning (SYNONYM) to "RIGID":
explanation: "Rigid" means unable to be bent or not flexible; its direct synonym is "inflexible".

subject: English
question_text: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning (ANTONYM) to "CONVERGE":
explanation: "Converge" means to tend to meet at a point; its exact opposite is "diverge" (to move apart in different directions).

subject: English
question_text: Choose the word closest in meaning (SYNONYM) to "LUCID":
explanation: "Lucid" describes writing, thought, or perception that is expressed clearly and easy to understand.

subject: English
question_text: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning (ANTONYM) to "PERPETUAL":
explanation: "Perpetual" means never ending or changing; "transitory" means brief or lasting for only a short time.

subject: English
question_text: Choose the word closest in meaning (SYNONYM) to "AMPLIFY":
explanation: "Amplify" means to increase the volume, scope, or intensity of something; its synonym is "magnify".

subject: English
question_text: Choose the word closest in meaning (SYNONYM) to "PERFUNCTORY":
explanation: "Perfunctory" denotes an action carried out with minimal effort, reflection, or interest; synonymous with cursory.

subject: English
question_text: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning (ANTONYM) to "EPHEMERAL":
explanation: "Ephemeral" means lasting for a very short time. Its direct antonym is "enduring" (permanent or long-lasting).

subject: English
question_text: Choose the word closest in meaning (SYNONYM) to "INEFFABLE":
explanation: "Ineffable" means too great or extreme to be expressed or described in words; inexpressible or indescribable.

subject: English
question_text: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning (ANTONYM) to "ZEALOUS":
explanation: "Zealous" means having or showing strong, energetic fervor; its antonym is "apathetic" (showing or feeling no enthusiasm or concern).

subject: English
question_text: Choose the word closest in meaning (SYNONYM) to "TACITURN":
explanation: "Taciturn" refers to a person reserved or uncommunicative in speech; synonymous with "reticent".

subject: English
question_text: Choose the word closest in meaning (SYNONYM) to "OBDURATE":
explanation: "Obdurate" describes someone stubbornly refusing to change their opinion or course of action; "intransigent" is its precise synonym.

subject: English
question_text: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning (ANTONYM) to "ESOTERIC":
explanation: "Esoteric" refers to knowledge intended for or likely to be understood by only a specialized few; its formal opposite is "exoteric" (suitable for or communicated to the general public).

subject: English
question_text: Choose the word closest in meaning (SYNONYM) to "PUSILLANIMOUS":
explanation: "Pusillanimous" means showing a lack of courage or resolution; timid. "Craven" is an exact synonym.

subject: English
question_text: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning (ANTONYM) to "SYCOPHANTIC":
explanation: "Sycophantic" describes behaving in an obsequious way in order to gain advantage; its antonym is being "unyieldingly candid" or frank.

subject: English
question_text: Choose the word closest in meaning (SYNONYM) to "PELLUCID":
explanation: "Pellucid" means translucently clear in surface or easily understood in meaning and style; synonymous with limpid and transparent.

subject: English
question_text: Choose the grammatically correct version of the sentence:
options: Each of the experimental trials yields consistent numerical data.
Each of the experimental trials yield consistent numerical data.
Each of the experimental trial yielding consistent numerical data.
Each of the experimental trials are yielding consistent numerical data.
explanation: "Each" is an indefinite singular pronoun requiring the singular verb "yields".

subject: English
question_text: Correct the error in comparison: "The computational power of modern GPUs is much higher than CPUs."
options: The computational power of modern GPUs is much higher than that of CPUs.
The computational power of modern GPUs is much higher then CPUs.
The computational power of modern GPUs are much higher than CPUs.
The computational power of modern GPUs is more higher than CPUs.
explanation: To prevent an illogical comparison between "computational power" and "CPUs", the demonstrative pronoun "that of" must be inserted.

subject: English
question_text: Select the sentence with proper punctuation:
options: The laboratory was stocked with beakers, pipettes, and burettes; however, the autoclave was malfunctioning.
The laboratory was stocked with beakers, pipettes, and burettes, however the autoclave was malfunctioning.
The laboratory was stocked with beakers, pipettes and burettes however, the autoclave was malfunctioning.
The laboratory was stocked with beakers pipettes and burettes; however the autoclave was malfunctioning.
explanation: Two independent clauses joined by the conjunctive adverb "however" require a semicolon before "however" and a comma after it.

subject: English
question_text: Correct the pronoun agreement: "Every researcher must submit their preliminary abstract by Friday."
options: Every researcher must submit his or her preliminary abstract by Friday.
Every researcher must submit their own preliminary abstracts by Friday.
Every researchers must submit his preliminary abstract by Friday.
Every researcher must submit them preliminary abstract by Friday.
explanation: In formal traditional grammar, "Every researcher" is singular and takes the singular pronoun phrase "his or her".

subject: English
question_text: Choose the sentence that corrects the double negative:
options: The sensors could scarcely register any ambient vibrations.
The sensors couldn't scarcely register any ambient vibrations.
The sensors couldn't register no ambient vibrations.
The sensors couldn't scarcely register no ambient vibrations.
explanation: "Scarcely" is already negative; combining it with "could not" or "no" forms an ungrammatical double negative.

subject: English
question_text: Identify the sentence that resolves the dangling modifier: "Running the simulation at peak load, the CPU overheated immediately."
options: When the engineer ran the simulation at peak load, the CPU overheated immediately.
Running the simulation at peak load, immediate overheating of the CPU occurred.
Running the simulation at peak load, overheating occurred in the CPU.
The CPU running the simulation at peak load overheated immediately.
explanation: The original sentence implies the CPU was "running the simulation". Adding the logical subject ("When the engineer ran...") eliminates the dangling modifier.

subject: English
question_text: Choose the sentence that eliminates the misplaced modifier:
options: The technician examined the telescope with a defective optical lens.
With a defective optical lens, the technician examined the telescope.
The technician examined with a defective optical lens the telescope.
